title: Bounded support of residue-fibre Betti numbers
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], E an object of its derived category [def-pc-derived-category], and x a point of X. Suppose there is an open V containing x and a strictly perfect complex P [def-pc-perfect-complex] on V whose derived object is isomorphic to the restriction of E. There are integers a and b such that for every i with i < a or b < i, the derived residue-fibre Betti number of E at x [def-sc-derived-fiber-betti] is zero.

proof.text: Choose the open V, strictly perfect complex P and restriction isomorphism. Take the original bounds a,b from IsStrictlyPerfect. The residue morphism g has constant value x, hence its inverse image of V is the whole spectrum W. Transport P through Modules.overEquiv V to a complex C on V.toScheme; additivity preserves its zero terms and the equivalence identifies the finite free sheaves with free sheaves of the same ranks.

Equip the sheaf-module category with the tensor-closed structure of lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed. Finite free sheaves are coproducts of the tensor unit and are flat by ObjectProperty.flat_coproduct and ObjectProperty.prop_unit. Apply ObjectProperty.flat_of_retract to the transported retraction maps to prove every term of C flat. This is the proved private helper flat_of_finiteFree_retract and its application to C.

Use standard derived categories on the open subschemes, independently of the ambient localization universe. Apply lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback to g.resLE V W and C. Its additive ordinary functor F gives the explicit complex FC termwise. Compose its Qh comparison with quotientCompQhIso and mapHomotopyCategoryFactors to obtain Lf*(Q(C)) isomorphic to Q(FC). Map the given local derived isomorphism through the open-site equivalence. The universe-aware open-restriction comparison identifies (S followed by B).mapDerivedCategory(Lg*E) with Q(FC), where S restricts to W and B is its over equivalence.

For i outside [a,b], FC.X i is zero because both A and F preserve zero objects. ShortComplex.isZero_homology_of_isZero_X₂ makes its homology zero. Transfer through the displayed derived isomorphism and homologyFunctorFactors. Restriction to W=top is faithful: equality of restricted maps evaluated on Over.mk(U→top) is equality of the original maps on U. The equivalence B is faithful too, so the faithful exact functor S followed by B reflects vanishing of derived homology. Evaluation and scalar restriction are additive and preserve zero objects; no exactness of evaluation is needed. The residue cohomology module is therefore subsingleton and Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton gives the required Betti-number zero. The original a,b work also for a>b and zero complexes.

proof_origin.place: First paragraph of proof, expanded using strictly perfect complexes (08C4), flat computation of derived pullback (06YJ), and open restriction (08DW); the Lean proof transfers zero cohomology sheaves, so evaluation exactness is unnecessary.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteFiberCohomologyBounded
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    [∀ x : X, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (moduleRings (Spec (X.residueField x)).toRingedSpace))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (x : X)
    (hlocal : ∃ V : X.Opens, x ∈ V ∧
      ∃ P : CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V)) ℤ,
        IsStrictlyPerfect X V P ∧
        Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
          (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) V).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)) :
    ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → derivedFiberBetti X E i x = 0
